description: A 30-episode grand tour of everything an optometrist encounters from the moment a patient sits down to the final prescription — exam workflow, history, acuity, pupils, motility, slit lamp, fundus, refraction, and prescribing.

episodes.title: The First 60 Seconds: Building Patient Rapport in Eye Exams
episodes.description:
What happens before you touch the slit lamp may be the most diagnostically powerful moment of your entire eye exam. In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we explore how the opening sixty seconds of an optometric encounter directly shape the quality of your patient history, the reliability of your clinical findings, and the accuracy of your differential diagnosis.

Designed exclusively for licensed optometrists, residents, and eye care professionals, this episode breaks down the clinical strategy behind patient rapport — not as a soft skill, but as a precision diagnostic tool. You will learn how your exam room environment influences patient disclosure, why open-ended questioning outperforms traditional intake questions, and how careful observation before retinoscopy or IOP measurement can surface critical findings like subtle ptosis, reduced blink rate, photophobia, or signs of fourth nerve palsy hiding in plain sight.

We cover how a well-structured verbal opening can surface buried chief complaints — the flashes and floaters a patient almost did not mention, the monocular blur that shifts your differential toward macular pathology, the night halos that point toward early cataract or elevated intraocular pressure. Every topic connects directly to your slit lamp exam, fundus evaluation, OCT decision-making, and clinical management priorities.

Whether you are a seasoned clinician refining your chairside technique or a resident building your clinical foundation, this episode delivers immediately applicable strategies for smarter, faster, and more complete optometric care.

Listen now and bring something genuinely useful into your practice tomorrow. Find more clinical episodes built for eye care professionals at Focuslinks.in.

episodes.title: Contrast Sensitivity: Why 20/20 Patients Still Struggle to See
episodes.description:
Your patient reads the 20/20 line without hesitation — then tells you they can't drive at night. Sound familiar? In this clinical episode of Focus Cast, we go beyond the Snellen chart to explore contrast sensitivity: the hidden dimension of functional vision that standard acuity testing consistently fails to capture.

Designed exclusively for optometrists, residents, and eye care clinicians, this episode delivers a practical, evidence-based deep dive into contrast sensitivity testing and its direct application at the chair. We cover the contrast sensitivity function (CSF), how to use the Pelli-Robson chart effectively, and when to reach for more comprehensive tools like the CSV-1000 or FACT chart.

You'll walk away with a clear differential diagnosis framework — from residual refractive error and media opacities like nuclear sclerotic and posterior subcapsular cataracts, to macular disease, keratoconus, glaucomatous ganglion cell loss, and optic neuritis. We connect contrast sensitivity deficits to your slit lamp findings, OCT interpretation, visual field protocols, and referral decision-making for cataract surgery, corneal crosslinking, and glaucoma co-management.

This is the clinical conversation your frustrated 20/20 patients have been waiting for you to have — and the testing tool that finally gives them an answer.

Visit Focus Cast at Focuslinks.in for more evidence-based clinical content built specifically for optometric practice. Keep looking deeper.
